_authority: The Instructor-Led Course Development Guideline: the teaching rules every Novikontas instructor-led module must meet - STCW, GWO, OPITO and in-house, in the classroom, at the drill ground, on the simulator and in team training. It sets what the factory's outputs must contain and adds four paper items: the pre-brief card, the debrief card, the observation card and the employer sheet. Law L68. Read by scripts/instructor_led.py, compile/scripts/module_plan.py and compile/scripts/additional_materials.py. How the course's own file is written: instructor-led/GUIDE.md. Edit this file, not the scripts.
_freeze: The guideline changes only when a real module fails without the change. A failure found in the field is logged against the rule that caused it, and only then is the rule changed. The same holds here: a limit in this file moves only with a module that failed without it.
_claims: Almost none of the guideline's evidence was measured on seafarers or wind technicians: numbers are quoted as 'in comparable training', and course documents claim behaviour change, never accident reduction.

R1.rule: Never reword a regulator's outcome. Add sub-outcomes beside it, each with a verb an assessor can see: checks, decides, orders, dons, reports, refuses - never 'understands' or 'is familiar with'.
R1.test: Original wording copied verbatim; every sub-outcome verb is observable.

R2.rule: Every sub-outcome has one dominant task type: fixed sequence, decision, real-time judgement or team behaviour. It picks the TLA. A blended exercise stays whole; split it only if two parts need different TLAs.
R2.test: One dominant task type per row of the outcome register.
R2.where: the course's instructor_led.json 'register'; module plan; instructor_led.py check

R3.rule: A fact is must-know only if, when it matters on board, there is no aid at hand or no time to use it. Everything else is practised with the aid in hand: SDS, checklist, manual.
R3.test: Must-know facts are listed; every other fact names its aid.

R4.rule: Active means every trainee commits to an output: a written answer, a card vote, a tablet answer, a pair answer or a performed step. The instructor asking the room and taking three or four answers is passive.
R4.test: Every active row names the output and who produces it.
R4.where: L5; active-learning.json; instructor_led.py check (the slide's notes)

R5.rule: Passive segment: one concept, then one trainee output. 15 minutes maximum.
R5.test: No passive run in the plan is longer than 15 minutes.
R5.where: L49; instructor_led.py check; module plan face

R6.rule: At least 80 % of theory minutes are active. Below 80 % the plan carries a one-line justification, which the reviewer may reject. Novices meeting a concept for the first time and second-language groups are valid reasons.
R6.test: The plan shows the passive % and, if over 20 %, the justification.

R7.rule: Active theory counts as theory hours. A tablet task counts as a practical hour only where the detailed plan lists a practical hour for that topic. The programme sets the minimum hours per topic; Novikontas sets the theory/practical split in its detailed plan.
R7.test: Hours in the module plan match the theory/practical split per topic.
R7.where: L1, L3, L34; module plan face

R8.rule: Every drill, simulator run and scenario runs brief, then show (first exposure only), then do, then debrief, all inside the allocated minutes. Pre-brief 3-5 min. Debrief 15-20 min per team drill or simulator run. A simple motor error gets a 30-second correction, not a full debrief.
R8.test: Brief and debrief appear as timed rows.
R8.where: 'practicals' cycle; module plan running order; instructor_led.py check

R9.rule: Every trainee performs every critical skill personally, at least twice after the first correct run. The recorded run is a later run under a changed condition, ideally the next day.
R9.test: Practice runs and the recorded run are separate rows.

R10.rule: During a run the instructor watches, records and stays quiet. Exceptions: the safety stop (anyone, any time, the stop word on the pre-brief card); freeze and restart when the run has left its objective; role-play voices that drive the scenario; short stop-and-go coaching on a novice's first runs of a drill sequence.
R10.test: Each run's card states the intervention rule.

R11.rule: Tablet tasks can use any HTML interaction. Each item makes the trainee commit to a decision, marked automatically the same way every time. Revealing, rotating or dragging content with no answer does not count.
R11.test: Every tablet item names its decision and how it is marked.
R11.where: L38; the build grades every item (review_sheets.mjs, 2.74.1)

R12.rule: Practicals are assessed by observation on the assessment form. Written items are vignettes or key-feature problems. Six to eight must-pass items per course. The final test meets the programme's minimum item count and the 70 % pass mark.
R12.test: Assessment form attached; must-pass items marked in the key.
R12.where: 'practicals' form; 'must_pass'; instructor_led.py check; the final's pass mark (L27)

limits._sub_outcomes: A house convention, not an evidence-based figure: about one sub-outcome per allocated hour, 3-5 per outcome. More than five per outcome means criteria are being written as sub-outcomes - merge them. Flagged when a module's sub-outcomes are more than 1.5 per allocated hour, rounded up.
limits._cycle: brief and debrief are rows inside the exercise's own minutes: the cycle's rows add up to the exercise screen's minutes exactly (R8). A debrief is a team debrief when the practical is 'team': true.

fixed_sequence.produces: Steps done with the hands, in order
fixed_sequence.evidence: Real equipment or a part-task trainer
fixed_sequence.never: One run each; watching counts as nothing

decision.label: Decision
decision.produces: What to check, refuse or call
decision.evidence: The cheapest that works: tablet, cards, vignette, paper tabletop
decision.never: Clicking or revealing with no committed answer

real_time_judgement.label: Real-time judgement
real_time_judgement.produces: Action ahead of a slow, lagging system
real_time_judgement.never: Free play; coaching mid-run; full-replay debrief

commit._what: R4 on a slide marked active: what makes it count. A slide whose own fields ask every trainee for an answer (a vote between choices, a true-or-false claim, a quick drill) commits by itself. Otherwise the instructor notes must say what every trainee produces - one of the 'yes' words - and a note that only asks the room ('no' words, with no 'yes' word) is the passive kind the guideline found. Words in the course language; matched case-insensitively as the start of a word. 'Predict' alone is not a yes: a class can predict aloud.

claims._what: Course documents claim behaviour change, never accident reduction. A slide, note or employer-sheet line matching one of these is reported.

tla_pool._what: The TLA Pool and Modality Matrix: 28 teaching and learning activities, at most five per Bloom level, indexed by task type with Bloom as a tag. A TLA enters only when a real module fails without it, and one leaves when one enters. Route: Practice = feedback only; Scored = counts toward pass or fail. In-class TLAs are Practice; the same formats become Scored only in the recorded run or the final paper. Every TLA that feeds a scored item has a refresher version for experienced trainees: the scenario first, the foundations skipped, a teach-back role. The names go into the method column of the detailed plan.

formats._what: 2.128.0 (Aigars Kluga, 2026-11-11: 'the factory is good but cannot vary - fine for one-direction courses like Gas, but narrow'). How each TLA of the pool is WRITTEN in a content script, so the factory chooses the format while it writes a module, not after. scripts/activity_formats.py reads it: a Sub-ILO's task type (the register's, or read from its verb with 'verbs') picks one or two TLAs near its Bloom level, varied across the module (instructor_led.py plan); an activity screen names its format ("format": the key); instructor_led.py draft turns every activity that is a drill, a team scenario or a project block ("practical": true) into a practical with cycle rows inside its minutes; content_script.py flags a module whose activities are all one format (a_one_direction) or whose team, real-time or hands-on Sub-ILO has no activity of its kind (a_type_unserved). 'drafts': slide (an active slide's fields), activity (an activity screen - the room), task (a tablet task's mechanic), feature (part of a team practical: its observers, its debrief). 'only': picked only when the Sub-ILO's verb is one of these, or for an EXPERIENCED course. The pool itself (tla_pool) is the guideline's and is not changed here.

verbs._how: The task type read from a Sub-ILO's words when the register does not set it: the EARLIEST of these verbs in the text decides (English; -s, -es, -ed, -d, -ing added). A text with none of them is a decision. Only a draft - the operator confirms the register (R2).

core._how: The format the task type's own evidence names (task_types 'evidence'): one closer in the picking score, so a real-time outcome gets the scenario run first and a hands-on outcome the demonstration, unless the module has used it already.

slide_active._how: An active slide's technique as a format: what the one-direction check counts.

slide_fields._how: A slide field that makes it a format by itself.

one_direction._how: A must-fix at script time (content_script.py a_one_direction): at least min_activities activity screens all of one format, or at least min_moments practice moments (activity screens and active slides) all of one format. "formats_why" at the top of the script keeps it a note. An activity screen with no "format" and no sign word is the format 'exercise' - two of them are one direction.

unnamed.label: an exercise of no named format

defaults.roles_solo: Each trainee works alone; the instructor walks round and watches.
defaults.roles_team: Teams of three or four perform; another team observes with the observation card; the instructor plays the outside roles.
safety_room: No real equipment is operated in this exercise.
Anyone may say the stop word; the exercise stops at once.
defaults.observe_unnamed: Every trainee produces their own output in the time
defaults.debrief_team_what: trainee-led: the observers first, then prompts 1 and 2

retrieval-round.tla: Decision-worded retrieval round, with the answer and reason given straight after
retrieval-round.write: a slide with "drill": "quick-fire" (lines "prompt | answer", each prompt a yes/no decision), or a self-check of single_choice questions whose feedback gives the reason

confusable-sort.write: a self-check with "mechanic": "categorise" - the items that are confused with each other, sorted into their groups

number-drill.tla: Number drill: each critical number recalled correctly three times, retested on a later day
number-drill.write: a self-check of number-entry questions ("set_value"), the same numbers again in a later module's check

vocabulary.write: a self-check with "mechanic": "match" - term to meaning, from the course glossary

explain-why.tla: Explain-why question after each concept block
explain-why.write: "active": "explain-then-reveal" after the concept block; the notes say each trainee writes the why before the reveal

predict-reveal.write: "active": "predict-then-reveal", the incident as the lines, "ask" the prediction, "reveal" what happened; each trainee writes or votes the prediction first

refutation.tla: Refutation card ('many think ... this is wrong because ... in fact ...')
refutation.write: "claim": the wrong belief, "claim_is": "false"; the lines say why it is wrong and what is true

contrast-pair.tla: Contrast pair: two cases, 'what do they share?'
contrast-pair.write: two cases side by side (build sheet "figure_b" and "blocks"), "ask": what do they share?, "reveal" the shared cause; each trainee writes first

teach-back.write: an active slide whose notes name the trainee who teaches it back and what the others check

worked-example.tla: Worked example, then faded steps, then solo
worked-example.write: "active": "worked-example", lines "what you do | what you get", "ask" the room's own turn with one step left out, "reveal" its answer

walkthrough.tla: Procedure walk-through with the aid in hand
walkthrough.write: an activity screen: pairs walk the procedure on paper with the real aid (checklist, permit, manual) in hand
walkthrough.roles: Pairs: one walks the procedure aloud with the aid in hand, the other checks each step against the aid; then they swap.
walkthrough.observe: Each step is checked against the aid, not done from memory

key-feature.write: a question on the step where people usually go wrong, answered with a verb (check, order, decide) - single or multi choice, kept for the final

hazard-map.tla: Hazard-chain map, built across the week
hazard-map.write: an activity screen: each pair adds today's property -> hazard -> control links to the map on the wall

case-dilemma.write: "active": "scenario", the case as the lines, "ask" go or no-go, "choices", one "why" each and "right"; or a tablet scenario that branches

write-plan.tla: Write the plan or brief (only where the outcome says prepare, plan or draft)
write-plan.write: an activity screen (a project block): each trainee writes the plan, brief or permit the outcome names, from the course's own data; pairs check it against the checklist
write-plan.roles: Each trainee writes their own; pairs swap and check each other's against the checklist.
write-plan.observe: The plan holds what the outcome asks for, from the course's own data

sequence-rebuild.write: a self-check with "mechanic": "order" - the procedure's steps to put in order

demonstration.write: an activity screen at the equipment or part-task trainer: the instructor shows at speed, then slowly with each step said; a trainee talks the instructor through it; then each trainee performs it, saying each step
demonstration.roles: Groups of up to six at one set: the instructor demonstrates, a trainee talks the instructor through it, then each trainee performs while saying each step.
demonstration.observe: Each step said before it is done, in the order of the procedure
demonstration.intervention: Stop-and-go coaching on each trainee's first run of the sequence (R10); after that I watch and stay quiet.

desktop-sim.write: an activity screen at the desktop simulator: each trainee does the procedure on it
desktop-sim.roles: Each trainee at a desktop simulator; the instructor walks round.
desktop-sim.observe: The steps done in order on the simulator, without prompting

planted-defect.write: an activity screen: each trainee inspects the real equipment; the instructor has planted one defect
planted-defect.roles: Each trainee inspects alone; one defect is planted, unknown to the trainee; the next trainee waits out of sight.
planted-defect.observe: The planted defect found and the item taken out of use

rewrite-procedure.tla: Rewrite the procedure after a failed run
rewrite-procedure.write: an activity screen after a run: each pair rewrites the step that failed and says why

fault-finding.write: an activity screen at the simulator or part-task trainer: a fault is set; the trainee finds it from the readings
fault-finding.roles: Pairs at the trainer: one finds the fault, the other records each reading and the time; then they swap.
fault-finding.observe: Readings checked before acting; the fault named from them

scenario-run.tla: Scenario run with two to four planned critical events
scenario-run.write: an activity screen: the team runs a scenario on the simulator or in the room; "events": the two to four planned critical events, each with its time or trigger; observers from another team
scenario-run.roles: Teams of three or four run the scenario; another team observes with the observation card; the instructor drives the planned events and plays the outside voices.
scenario-run.observe: Each planned event acted on before it escalates
scenario-run.intervention: I freeze and restart only if the run leaves its objective; the outside voices are mine.

critique.write: two track plots, plans or recordings side by side ("figure_b"), "ask" which is better and why, "reveal" the standard; each trainee writes first

design-scenario.write: an activity screen: pairs write an event set - the trigger, a distracter, what good looks like

closed-loop.write: an activity screen (a room drill or role-play): one gives orders, one reads back and acts, one observes; roles rotate each run
closed-loop.roles: Groups of three: one gives the orders, one reads back and acts, one observes with the observation card; the roles rotate each run.
closed-loop.observe: Every order read back and confirmed before it is acted on

observer-role.tla: Structured observer role during another team's run
observer-role.write: in a team practical's roles: another team observes with the observation card and speaks first in the debrief

challenge-response.tla: Challenge-and-response against a senior who pushes back
challenge-response.write: an activity screen (a role-play): a senior (the instructor, or a trainee with a script) pushes back; the trainee challenges until the hazard is answered; a third trainee observes
challenge-response.roles: Trios: one plays the senior who pushes back (from the instructor's script), one challenges, one observes with the observation card; the roles rotate.
challenge-response.observe: The challenge repeated and raised until the senior answers it

trainee-debrief.write: a team practical's debrief row: the trainees lead it, the observers first

cards._what: The four paper items (guideline 5.3, 5.4, 5.5 and 5.6), one page each, made by additional_materials.py from the course's approved instructor_led.json into course\additional-materials\practical-kit\. One pre-brief card, debrief card and observation card per drill, simulator run or team scenario (role-play included) - not for tablet tasks, cases or classroom discussions. An assessment form per recorded run. One employer sheet per course.
cards.intervention_default: I will watch and stay quiet. I stop the run only for safety or if it leaves its objective.

debrief_default.reactions: "How did that go?" The trainees speak first, juniors before seniors.
debrief_default.prompt_1: "At [time or step], what did you see, and what did you decide?"
debrief_default.feedback: Name the behaviour, the standard and the next action. Never praise or rank the person.
debrief_default.close: "One change for the next run." Each trainee says theirs.

cards.decision: Yes / Not yet. One sentence of justification for any Not yet.
cards.run_details: Practice runs completed (count) · the changed condition of this recorded run · attempt 1 / 2 / 3 (two re-attempts at most) · assessor (not the trainer, where possible) · date · signatures
cards.decay_default: In comparable training, procedural accuracy loses about half its gain in 6.5 months.

checklist.item: Every regulator outcome is copied verbatim, with its source and theory/practical hours
checklist.by: L2 - ilo_map.py and the Stage 2 page

checklist.item: Every sub-outcome has an observable verb and one dominant task type
Must-know facts are few and listed; everything else is practised with the aid in hand
Sub-outcome count is within budget: about one per allocated hour, 3-5 per outcome
Every sub-outcome passes the job and evidence tests, and its evidence is named
Every must-pass criterion has its own form step
Minutes add up to the allocation, and the header shows the passive %
Every Active row names the output and states that every trainee produces it
No passive segment is longer than 15 min, and each is followed by an output
Passive share is 20 % or less, or a one-line justification is given
Tablet tasks counted as practical only where the programme lists practical hours for that outcome
checklist.by: L49 - tablet tasks are theory minutes taught by doing; the programme's practical hours are never changed

checklist.item: Every drill, run and scenario has timed Brief and Debrief rows, and Show on first exposure
Practice runs and the recorded run are separate; the recorded run is later and under a changed condition
Every run's card states the intervention rule and the stop word
Theory days open with decision-worded retrieval, and each concept block ends with a why-question
Every known misconception is refuted with a case; every demonstration has a written prediction first
No decorative photos or sea stories; slides carry key terms, not the spoken text
Every tablet item names the decision it asks for and how it is marked
checklist.by: L38 - the build grades every question right and wrong (review_sheets.mjs)

checklist.item: Every assessed practical has an assessment form: 8-12 critical steps including stop criteria, global rating, Yes / Not yet
Written items are vignette or key-feature items; must-pass items are marked; three surface variants per decision
checklist.by_hand: vignette or key-feature; the three surface variants

checklist.item: No scored item depends on written English beyond the terms the job requires
No AI or peer score counts toward pass or fail
checklist.by: L27 - only the final assessment is graded

checklist.item: Pre-brief, debrief and observation cards exist for every drill, run and scenario
Glossary and misconception list are updated with this module's entries
The employer sheet names the fastest-decaying skills and one on-board drill
Course documents claim behaviour change, not accident reduction
